tuner_timing.justification: To minimize latency, I'm aggressively reducing scheduler latencies, enabling NAPI busy polling, and restricting C-states to POLL to keep cores active. I'm also increasing migration cost to keep tasks on the same CPU to reduce cache misses.
Lowering latency_ns has consistently reduced latency_p99 in previous iterations. Further decreasing it will test if this trend continues to yield better performance.

Continuing the trend of reducing CFS scheduler latency, we are setting latency_ns to its minimum value to observe if further improvements in p99 latency can be achieved. The cstate_max remains at POLL to ensure minimal idle latency.

With CFS latency_ns at its minimum, we are now exploring other parameters. Introducing napi_busy_poll aims to reduce network-related latency, and decreasing min_granularity_ns will test if finer scheduling granularity further improves responsiveness for this noisy workload.
We are further reducing scheduling granularities and increasing napi_busy_poll to exploit the promising region found in previous iterations for improved latency.

Iteration 9 showed a regression in latency when min_granularity_ns and wakeup_granularity_ns were reduced to 250,000. Reverting these to the previously best performing value of 500,000 aims to confirm the optimal point and improve latency.

We are exploring the impact of migration cost on latency, as other core scheduling parameters have shown a sweet spot. Reducing migration_cost_ns might allow for more efficient task balancing across cores, potentially lowering p99 latency.

Reverting to the best performing configuration (Iter 8) and exploring a higher value for napi_busy_poll may further reduce network-related latency by decreasing interrupt overhead. We are aiming to confirm robustness and find potential further improvements.

Re-evaluating the best performing configuration from Iteration 8 to confirm its robustness and account for measurement noise, especially since recent trials and a repeat of this config (Iteration 10) showed higher latency. This strategy helps to stabilize around the optimal region.

Given the noisy workload and the current performance fluctuation, I am exploring the minimum allowed value for migration_cost_ns to investigate if further reducing task migration overhead can improve latency_p99. Other parameters are kept at values that yielded the best performance so far.

Given the significant noise observed and the variability in reproducing the best performance, we are returning to the parameters of the best-performing configuration (Iter 8) and exploring a slightly lower value for 'napi_busy_poll' to refine the optimal region. This systematic adjustment helps understand its impact on latency.

Given the recent degradation with napi_busy_poll=100, we are reverting to the value of 200 which yielded the best performance (3.15) in iteration 8. This aims to re-validate the optimal region and mitigate the impact of noise.

Given the current best configuration is showing variability due to noise, we are slightly increasing migration_cost_ns to explore if further discouraging CPU migrations can stabilize or improve latency.

Reverting to the configuration that previously yielded the best latency_p99 (3.15) to confirm its robustness and performance, given the noisy workload and recent performance degradation. This step aims to re-validate the optimal parameter set.

Given the recent degradation of the historically best configuration, we are re-exploring a previously stable and high-performing configuration (Iter 7, latency_p99=3.30) to assess its robustness under current system conditions. This strategy aims to find a more resilient optimal point amidst noise.

The previous best result was achieved with specific scheduling parameters. To further minimize latency, I will explore setting min_perf_pct to 100 to keep CPU cores at their highest frequency, which typically reduces latency for demanding workloads.

The recent latency increase in Iter 22 coincided with setting `min_perf_pct` to 100 and higher granularity settings. Reverting to the parameters of Iter 8 (the best performing configuration so far) to confirm its robustness and re-evaluate its performance.

Given the recent noisy measurements and a higher p99 latency with the previous best configuration, we are re-exploring a slightly different setting from a previously good result (iter 11, 3.39) by lowering migration_cost_ns to see if it yields more stable or improved latency.

Reverting to the historically best-performing configuration (Iter 8) to re-evaluate its stability and robustness, especially after a period of noisy and less optimal results. This helps confirm the previous optimum and mitigate the impact of workload variability.

The best observed performance was with migration_cost_ns=500000, and another good result was with 250000. This configuration explores an intermediate value for migration_cost_ns to refine the optimal point, while keeping other parameters at their best performing values.

Reverting migration_cost_ns to 500,000 as this was the value in the best performing configuration (Iter 8) which yielded 3.15. This step aims to re-evaluate the parameter's impact and confirm the stability of the best configuration given the noisy workload.

Reverting to the historically best configuration (Iter 8) to re-evaluate its performance and confirm stability, especially after recent iterations showed higher latency. This strategy helps to re-center around a known optimal point amidst measurement noise.

The best configuration from Iter 8 yielded a noisy, higher latency in Iter 28. To account for system variability and explore minor refinements around the optimal region, I am slightly increasing napi_busy_poll to test for robustness and potential improvement.

The best observed latency_p99 of 3.15 was achieved with napi_busy_poll=200. Recent explorations with other values for napi_busy_poll have resulted in higher latencies, so we are reverting to the historically best value to re-evaluate its performance amidst system noise.

The best observed latency_p99 (3.15) was achieved with these parameters. Re-applying this configuration to confirm its robustness and stability amidst recent noisy measurements, which have shown higher latency values.

The optimization has likely converged as repeated trials of the best configuration yield fluctuating results due to workload noise, and further parameter adjustments have not consistently surpassed the current best observed latency. We will re-apply the best performing configuration to confirm its robustness amidst the noise.

The best observed latency was achieved with specific parameters, and recent runs show variability likely due to noise. This step makes a small, incremental adjustment to napi_busy_poll to explore a finer granularity around the previous optimal point.

Given the noisy measurements and the fact that iteration 8 yielded the best latency_p99, I am re-testing this configuration to confirm its robustness and rule out measurement variability. This re-evaluation will help confirm if the previous best result was an outlier or if this parameter set is consistently optimal.
